description.value: The Sointula Museum traces the 125-year history of a Finnish socialist Utopian settlement on Malcolm Island, housed in the former Malcolm Island Superior School. Three exhibition rooms cover everything from Indigenous presence and early settler life to the fishing industry, a legendary town midwife, and a working 1905 fog-horn from Pulteney Point Lighthouse. Reaching Sointula requires a BC Ferries crossing, making the museum a natural anchor for cyclists exploring this remote island community between Vancouver Island and the BC mainland.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A well-established, operating non-profit museum that is the primary cultural attraction on Malcolm Island — a ferry-accessible cycling destination. Clear public benefit for touring cyclists visiting Sointula.
enrichment_extras.notes: Admission is by donation. The museum building also houses the Sointula Library, a dance studio, and a thrift store. Free parking is available in lots in front of and behind the building.

wow_evidence: Museum of the 1901 Finnish socialist utopian colony — one of BC's great oddball settlement stories; three rooms in the old school.
